lockedMove.speaker: Tom Jump
lockedMove.proposition: Reality cannot fail to be reality and one plus one cannot fail to equal two even without God, so divine presupposition is not required for those necessities.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: to presuppose God because reality can't not be reality. A can't not be a 1 plus 1 can't not be two. Even if there isn't a God. So if you want to say that you need to presuppose God to have those things to have the preconditions for intelligibility A= A 1 plus 1 equals 2 then you would need to show some possible way for those to be false if there wasn't a god which I don't think

lockedMove.speaker: Tom Jump
lockedMove.proposition: The impossibility of believing that one exists while being wrong supplies a self-validating starting point whose principle applies to thinkers, individual objects, and plurality.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: this principle, the fact that I can't believe I exist and be wrong applies not only to me but to anything that thinks and to any individual object and the math that can describe the individuality of me and the plurality of the other objects. So this one principle does describe the normative thing that applies to all of them. So the fact that I can't believe I exist and be wrong

response.rationale: This constructive move supplies indubitable first-person existence as an epistemic starting point and extends its principle to thinkers, objects, and plurality.
